sourcedFrom: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) (undated on cover)
cleanIntro: CVA's own cleaning procedure for the Cascade. The strip is one movement — safety back, bolt out past the bolt stop — and then the whole job is the bore and the bolt. ⛔ Two numbers in this book decide whether the rifle still shoots where it did: the action screws go back at 50-55 inch-pounds, and the cocking indicator must be visible whenever the bolt handle is down. And one chemical warning that is about the STOCK, not the steel: DEET destroys the soft-touch finish and CVA will not warrant it.

steps.title: Confirm it is unloaded — again
steps.action: Before anything else, check the rifle is unloaded. CVA asks for this at the top of the cleaning section even though you already cleared it to leave the range.
steps.prose: The book's reasoning is that the check before travelling home and the check before cleaning are two different checks, and only one of them happens at the bench.
steps.quote: NEVER transport a loaded rifle in your vehicle or take a loaded rifle into the home. Before beginning your cleaning process, check again to be certain that the gun is unloaded.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10
steps.warn: ALWAYS use eye protection when loading, shooting, or cleaning a firearm.

steps.title: Safety lever rearward to SAFE
steps.action: Rotate the safety lever rearward into the safe position before the bolt moves.
steps.prose: On a Cascade the safety is rearward for safe and forward for fire — the opposite convention to some bolt guns, so check the lever rather than assuming.
steps.quote: Rotate the safety lever rearward to the safe position.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 1

steps.title: Bolt back, press the bolt stop, bolt out
steps.action: Open the bolt and draw it fully rearward, press the BOLT STOP on the LEFT side of the receiver, and pull the bolt out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The bolt stop is a lever, not a button, and it is on the opposite side from the bolt handle — you press it with the hand that is not holding the bolt.
steps.quote: Open the bolt and move it to the rear. Press the bolt stop, located on the left side of the receiver, and pull the bolt out of the receiver.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 2

steps.title: Look through the bore from the breech
steps.action: With the bolt out, look through the barrel from the BREECH end and confirm there is no cartridge in the chamber and no obstruction in the bore.
steps.prose: This is the only moment the bore is visible end to end, and an obstruction found here is a nuisance rather than a burst barrel.
steps.quote: Visually examine the barrel, looking through it from the breech end to ensure that there is no cartridge in the chamber or obstruction in the bore.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 3
steps.warn: Check that the barrel is free from any obstruction before loading and firing.

steps.title: Solvent patch from the breech, then let it work
steps.action: Push a single solvent-soaked patch through the bore FROM THE BREECH END with a good rod and the correct calibre jag, and leave the solvent a minute or two to do its job.
steps.prose: Breech to muzzle, always — that is the direction the bullet went and the direction the crown wants the rod moving.
steps.quote: Using a good quality cleaning rod and the correct caliber jag and patch, push a single solvent-soaked patch through the bore from the breech end. Allow the solvent to work for a minute or two.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 5

steps.title: Dry patches until they come out clean
steps.action: Dry patch on the jag, through the bore, repeat several times until the patches come out relatively clean. If they will not clean up, or will not push smoothly, run a bronze brush through and go back to the solvent patch.
steps.prose: "Relatively" is CVA's word and it is honest — a bore that patches perfectly white is usually one that has been over-cleaned.
steps.quote: Place a dry patch on the cleaning jag and push it through the bore. Repeat several times until the patches come out relatively clean.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, steps 6-7

steps.title: ⛔ Bolt face, extractor and ejector — and keep DEET away
steps.action: Paper towel, rag and cotton swabs on the bolt, with particular attention to the RECESSED BOLT FACE where the extractor and ejector sit. Remove all fouling, rust and corrosion, then lube the bolt body, the three lugs, the threads and cocking cam, and the front and sides of the cocking piece.
steps.prose: ⛔ Keep harsh cleaners and insect repellent off the stock. CVA names DEET specifically — it attacks the soft-touch layer and the camo finish, and that damage is explicitly not warranted.
steps.quote: Using a paper towel or rag and some cotton swabs, thoroughly clean the bolt, paying special attention to the recessed bolt face where the extractor and ejector are located.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 9
steps.warn: To best preserve the camo finish and soft touch layer on your stock please avoid contact with harsh cleaning products and insect repellents containing diethyltoluamide

steps.title: ⛔ CVA's serial-number recall — printed in this book
steps.action: This manual carries CVA's 1997 VOLUNTARY RECALL. It applies to IN-LINE MUZZLELOADING RIFLES whose serial numbers end in -95 or -96 — not to the Cascade, which is a centrefire bolt-action. If you own any CVA in-line muzzleloader, read the serial number and check it now.
steps.prose: ⛔ A recalled gun must not be used or lent to anyone, by CVA's own words, and CVA replaces it free of charge. This is repeated here rather than left out because the rifle in your hands is not the only CVA in the safe, and the notice is printed in this book for a reason.
steps.aside: Example of a recalled serial number: 61-13-XXXXXX-95
steps.quote: If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line muzzleloader with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the rifle under any circumstances.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 15. VOLUNTARY RECALL OF CERTAIN CVA MUZZLELOADERS, printed p.11

steps.title: Bolt back in, then check trigger and safety
steps.action: Insert the bolt into the receiver, close it, and check the function of the trigger and the safety before the rifle goes away.
steps.prose: Anything that does not feel right here is a phone call to CVA, not an adjustment — the book says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Insert the bolt into the receiver, close the bolt, and check the function of the trigger and safety.
steps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 12

deepSteps.title: The bolt comes apart only if you need it to
deepSteps.action: CVA frames bolt disassembly as conditional — do it if you feel you need to, not as part of a routine clean. Have a strong pin, a small Allen key or a punch ready.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ CVA's own aside is worth repeating: a paper clip will not work here. The pin takes the full spring load of the firing pin assembly and a soft one bends into the hole.
deepSteps.quote: If you feel you need to disassemble the bolt, follow the steps below
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 10

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Unscrew the shroud counterclockwise — and stop there
deepSteps.action: With the pin holding the assembly, unscrew the firing pin assembly by turning the BOLT SHROUD counterclockwise, and lift the firing pin assembly out of the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ That is the end of the published procedure. CVA states plainly that further disassembly is not recommended, and the firing pin assembly is a spring-loaded unit that should stay a unit.
deepSteps.quote: Unscrew the firing pin assembly by turning the bolt shroud counterclockwise and remove the firing pin assembly from the bolt. Further disassembly is not recommended.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 10

deepSteps.title: Lubricate the shroud threads, reassemble in reverse
deepSteps.action: Lubricate the bolt shroud threads and put the assembly back together in reverse order.
deepSteps.prose: The threads are the only lubricated surface in the assembly; the firing pin itself stays dry so it does not slow in the cold.
deepSteps.quote: Lubricate the bolt shroud threads and assemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 10

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The check that says it went back correctly
deepSteps.action: When the bolt is reassembled, the firing pin should sit at the TOP of the bolt cam notch.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the pass/fail on the whole job. A firing pin sitting anywhere else means the assembly is not indexed and the rifle must not be closed on a cartridge.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin should sit at the top of the bolt cam notch as shown when complete.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 10

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Action screws back at 50-55 inch-pounds
deepSteps.action: If the stock came off during cleaning, tighten the retaining screws to 50 to 55 inch-pounds of torque on reassembly.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ This is the number that decides whether the zero survives the clean. Over-torqued screws stress the receiver, under-torqued ones let the action shift shot to shot.
deepSteps.quote: tighten the retaining screws to 50 to 55 inch-pounds of torque during reassembly.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 12. CLEANING AND MAINTAINING THE CASCADE, printed p.8-10, step 11

deepSteps.title: Trigger weight, if you adjust it — and the safety check after
deepSteps.action: The trigger is factory-set near 3 lb with roughly a 2-4 lb range. Take the two stock retaining screws out with a 5/32 inch or 4 mm hex key, lift the barrelled action from the stock, and turn the adjustment screw clockwise for heavier or counterclockwise for lighter, in small steps, testing with a gauge.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ After ANY adjustment, work the bolt vigorously and watch the cocking indicator. If the firing pin falls when the bolt handle is lowered, the rifle is unsafe — that is a call to CVA, not a further tweak. Action back in the stock at 55 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.aside: Place the barrel and receiver back into the stock and tighten the retaining screws to 55 inch-pounds.
deepSteps.quote: The cocking indicator should always be visible when the bolt handle is lowered. If the firing pin falls when the bolt handle is lowered contact CVA Customer Service immediately.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 6. ADJUSTING THE TRIGGER WEIGHT-OF-PULL, printed p.6

deepSteps.title: Barrel break-in, on a new rifle
deepSteps.action: For the first 5 shots, clean after EACH shot and after the barrel has cooled. For the next 50, clean every 10 shots, letting the barrel cool between. After that, clean carefully after each range or hunting trip.
deepSteps.prose: CVA's stated reason is that break-in smooths the microscopic tool marks left in a new bore, and that a broken-in barrel fouls less and cleans more easily afterwards. Avoid overheating it.
deepSteps.quote: For the first 5 shots, clean the rifle after each shot and after the barrel cools.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Cascade Instruction Manual (Cascade-Manual-3.2) — Cascade-Manual-3.2 (revision printed in the filename, not on the page) — 10. BARREL BREAK-IN PROCEDURE, printed p.7

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Solvent-soaked patch from the BREECH end, left a minute or two to work
Dry patches until they come out relatively clean; bronze brush only if they will not
Never force a rod that is not pushing smoothly

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Cotton swabs into the recessed bolt face, around the extractor and ejector
Remove all fouling, rust and corrosion before any oil goes on
Light oil on the bolt body, the three lugs, the threads and cocking cam, and the front and sides of the cocking piece

cleaning.name: STOCK & ACTION
tasks: ⛔ No harsh cleaners and no DEET-based insect repellent on the stock — chemical damage is not warranted
If the stock came off, action screws back at 50-55 inch-pounds
Wipe the magazine body and feed lips dry

reassembly: Reassemble the bolt in reverse order with the shroud threads lubricated, and confirm the firing pin sits at the top of the bolt cam notch.
If the stock was removed, refit the barrelled action and torque the retaining screws to 50-55 inch-pounds.
Insert the bolt into the receiver and close it.
Check the function of the trigger and safety before the rifle goes away.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, work the bolt several times and confirm the cocking indicator is visible whenever the bolt handle is down, and that the safety holds in the rearward position.
